utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, if it would assist you, before you started cross-examination on this point I already at paragraph 20 made a note for myself: See sources in footnote 24. So you are extensively dealing with it, which I do not mind, but if you would have put the last question to the witness and if the answer would have been the same you would have saved quite some time. So it was something that had already attracted the attention of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm always grateful for any help from the Trial Chamber. I'm not absolutely clear what it is Your Honour is suggesting I might cut out there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I make a note, see the sources in footnote 24, that is because it needs -- at least it came into my mind that the footnote might not give the support one would wish for that portion of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm grateful for that observation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then if -- under those circumstances, of course you are dealing with a professional Bench, then the point is made far more quickly than in front of a jury.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. And Your Honours are dealing with a professional advocate who does appreciate the difference between a jury and a professional Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, can we look at reports, then, because in fact the distinction in presentation which I suggest is one you make yourself very helpfully in the footnote, so you give examples of reporting to central organs, and here if we look first at the telex from the SDS Crisis Staff Bijeljina to, always a hard one that one, to SDS Main Board, that is in presentation, or I hope it is, presentation binder 2 at tab 45. And this is certainly on its face, Ms. Hanson, it is a report addressed to the SDS Main Board. That's what it says there. And it is certainly, at the foot, on its face sent from the or by the Crisis Staff of Bijeljina. That's what it says. It says, then, and I'm reading of course from the English at the top: "Report on the situation as at 2000 hours on 1st of April, 1992." And so on. "Inter-ethnic conflicts, signs possibly subsiding. A short time ago the National Defence Council of the Bijeljina municipality held a meeting at which the following conclusions were made." Ms. Hanson, where does the -- please explain. Where does the National Defence Council of the Bijeljina municipality fit in?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a municipal council consisting of, I believe, the president of the municipality, the secretary -- the secretary of -- municipal Secretariat for National Defence, probably the head of the municipal TO staff, other figures. I could -- I could get some more details on it, but it's an organ that existed all -- in the legislation of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia. It's a -- I mean, there were provisions for this in all municipalities, as far as I know, intended to discuss issues of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So this is -- the National Defence Council, then, was not in any sense, was it, a body established by the Bosnian Serb community?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this sentence, it's not clear. As we know, according to the 19 December instructions, when the Serbs formed their Serbian municipalities, they were to set up municipal organs. So it is possible that a Serb municipality had its own Serb municipal National Defence Council. At this time they just referred to it as the National Defence Council of the Bijeljina municipality. So I would read that to mean of the existing legal Bijeljina municipal government. So I would not take that to be a specifically SDS body.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And do you agree that that -- the contention that you just put forward would be, if anything, supported by item 1, that the leaders of the SDS and SDA shall address the citizens on Radio Bijeljina, and 3, that ethnically mixed patrols shall be formed of members of the JNA and SGB?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And -- well -- so the curfew, and His Honour Judge Hanoteau I think asked a question specifically relating to item 2, and that means of course that the curfew which is, on its face, isn't it applicable to all citizens without distinction was decided upon by that body, the National Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what this report indicates.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So accepting that on the face of this document it is in simple terms a report by the Crisis Staff of Bijeljina to the SDS Main Board, in fact all it does is report a decision of that other body altogether?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: And at the bottom it simply also notes that they will remain on the highest level of alert. They, the Crisis Staff, not the National Defence Council, is how I read that last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Then the next item in your footnote, Novo Sarajevo, is a -- what's described as a special session -- sorry, I didn't give the reference. Tab 46. That's presentation binder 2, tab 46. It's a special session of the Municipal Board, SDS Novo Sarajevo out of the room of the municipality Assembly, and the particular point to which you drew attention here related to the last couple of paragraphs where Mr. Andric is making a proposal. And then there's a -- there's a sort of mini debate going on, isn't there, involving Mr. Lackanovic and Mr. Andric; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And Mr. Lackanovic, my apologies to him in his absence if I'm not pronouncing it right, but Mr. Lackanovic states his opinion that the first item of the agenda should be discussed by the Assembly of the party. The first item on the agenda -- first of all, we don't see an agenda, do we?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he's referring to the sentences right above there. Andric's proposal for an agenda, because I don't see any other agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- invite your confirmation. There is no separate agenda. It is that proposed agenda coming from Mr. Andric. That's the way you read it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That seems the most logical reading there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then Mr. Lackanovic's proposal that should be discussed by the Assembly of the party. What do you -- what do you understand as being meant by the Assembly of the party in Mr. Lackanovic's comments?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the Assembly in the next paragraph specifies Bosnian Serb Assembly. Here I would take this to be most likely the Municipal Assembly of the party. The SDS had at the municipal level -- it had a party board, the Municipal Board, but there was also a Municipal Assembly of the members of the party or representatives of the party membership at the municipal level. It --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The -- yes, I'm sorry, I interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says the Assembly of the party and the next sentence says the Bosnian Serb Assembly. I think it's -- they seem to be making a distinction so I would -- there, but it's not completely clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Would you agree, the distinction between being made Mr. -- or the essential distinction between Mr. Lackanovic's proposal and Mr. Andric's proposal is that Mr. Lackanovic is saying that the matter should be discussed at the local level or the municipal level, and Mr. Andric is saying no, it -- the work should be discussed at the national level or the republic level?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think what they're doing here is dividing in two the problems contained in 1, problems within the party and the responsibility of the president, and Andric is making a distinction that the Municipal Board can discuss the problems of the president, Mr. Prijic. But as far as the work of the Crisis Staff, that is a matter for the republic level Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, I don't think there's any dispute between us. If we park on one side the issue of the discussion of the work of the president, Mr. Lackanovic is also suggesting that the Crisis Staff work should be discussed at the municipal -- at the municipal level, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Mr. Dobrilovic is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. I beg your pardon. Mr. Dobrilovic comes into the conversation. I'm so sorry. Yes, Mr. Dobrilovic makes that -- in that paragraph he makes that suggestion. Quite right. He makes that suggestion. It's discussed at the local level by the Assembly party, and Mr. Andric is saying no, it should be discussed at -- what do they call it, the national level.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I read this as an indication -- the time between the Crisis Staff and the Assembly level -- the national level. That's why I -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And when Mr. Andric refers to the Bosnian Serb Assembly having formed the Crisis Staff, he's actually wrong, isn't he, about that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's wrong in the extent that the 19 December instructions were apparently issued by the Main Board. We also see in Prijedor a reference to materials received from the Assembly that clearly are the 19 -- judging from the content, the 19 December instructions. So I have seen, not just here, some confusion on the -- where these instructions came from. As I said, there was a meeting of the Assembly on the 21st of December which may go to help to account for the confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: As you've indicated yourself, Ms. Hanson, it's not unusual to find confusion about legal, political structures, terminology, who is in charge of whom, who reports to whom. That's not at all unusual in everything you have examined, is it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen imprecision in the use of terms especially when the municipal level is referring to bodies at the republican level. As we saw, Deronjic refers to the Presidency of the SDS, and I don't believe there is such a body seen elsewhere in the SDS at the national level. So I assume precision, and it appears to be a reflection of either imprecise knowledge or general impression of the leadership is these bodies, and they -- that's where things come from but not precise about which precise body issued it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So -- but this is your first example in your footnote of a report by a Crisis Staff to an SDS central organ, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the second, I believe, because Bijeljina was the first.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's the second. The second, yes. Agreed?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But, Ms. Hanson, it's not a report to an SDS central organ by a Crisis Staff, is it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's an indication of an expectation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So it is not an example. It doesn't fit the footnote. It is not correctly an example of what it purports to be at all, is it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not an example of actual reporting here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Let's then turn on, please, to tab 71. It's conveniently in the same binder. Oh, I'm sorry. It is a switch to the master binder. We have to switch to the master binder on this one. It's master binder 2, tab 71. Do you have that, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: This is described in your report as the SDS Crisis Staff sending an appeal to Krajisnik and Karadzic, among others, to help resolve the particular crisis there mentioned.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, the document, and of course I'm working from the English, but I think you worked from the original B/C/S version, Ms. Hanson, the document is headed underneath the fax number and all that sort of stuff, "Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia-Herzegovina Municipal Board of Zivinice." So on the face of it it's from the Municipal Board; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's signed by the president of the SDS Municipal Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. And it is addressed not by name but of course it shows on its face that it's addressed among others -- to among others, the president of the Serb Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and there is no dispute that that was Mr. Krajisnik at the time, but for what reason do you describe it in your footnote as the SDS Crisis Staff sending an appeal to Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Karadzic -- or Dr. Karadzic, among others?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could quickly look at the second page. Well, as I said, it's signed by the president of the SDS, and he says that leaders of the SDS have formed a Crisis Staff. He says that on the first page. In order to negotiate with the authorities. And they describe the course of the negotiations, and they talk about what needs to be done to solve this problem. Perhaps an appeal is too strong, but it is a report on the negotiations and a request for some actions to resolve it. And since as we know according to the 19 December instructions the president of the SDS Municipal Board would be on the Crisis Staff, and it says that the leaders of the SDS have formed a Crisis Staff, I think that a reasonable conclusion that he is -- that Djuro Mihic is on this Crisis Staff that he describes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, you said that you referred to tab 71 of the master binder. What would that be in the presentation binder, if at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I don't think it was there, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It did not have a separate presentation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could in general terms would it be possible to link footnotes to the -- to the master binder, because it's beautiful if once you've found the document in the master binder that you see to what footnote it refers, but very often the Chamber would look at the report, would like to check the footnotes and the sources mentioned therein but is unable to find it -- or have I overlooked something, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I don't think we have -- we have that document before you. I think that's something we could create. We created our presentation spreadsheet which has references to both the presentation tab and the master tab numbers, but that does not include the items that are only in the master binders. But I think that's a document that we could easily create for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course the logical order for a Chamber is not to start to check the sources but first to start reading the report, and it's really difficult to --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We do have a set of the master binders here, Your Honour, but there's only one set.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's not at this moment my main problem because we -- but especially for working for us it would be far more convenient if we would have the sources related to whether it's master binder or presentation binder or --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If I understand correctly, Your Honour, what would be most helpful for you is a document that contained a cross-reference between each footnote and where it appears in the master binders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Exactly. Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We will provide that to you as soon as we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we're grateful for that response from Mr. Hannis. Can I say, Your Honour, we do have a number of suggestions but now is not the time to make them in light of experience of this witness and this evidence. The Defence has a number of practical suggestions that we will communicate to the Trial Chamber for whatever help they might possibly be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you'll first discuss them with the Prosecution and see whether you, together, could come to any practical solutions, and then the Chamber would be glad to receive them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We certainly will do that, Your Honour, because they would best involve a degree of cooperation and coordination between us, so we will certainly do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The -- Your Honour, can I just say, for purposes of my cross-examination, I have prepared on the basis that where something is in the presentation binders, that's the reference I have used, partly, Your Honour, for the sheer physical convenience that there are fewer of the presentation binders. The master binder use would involve far more documents being carried backwards and forwards and carried across court and so on. That's the reason I have done it, Your Honour. It is really a bit late for me to undo that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that's excellent because we have -- at least I took some of the presentation binders with me because they're easier to carry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- there's simply more. We all find the same there, Your Honour. Therefore, what I've done - and I don't claim a hundred per cent perfection on this; I don't think I usually do - but it's only where there isn't a presentation binder reference that I go to the master binder reference. That's my system anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's the best I can do, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Anyway, here we are at master binder 2, 71, still, and, Ms. Hanson, after that little discussion among the Judges and lawyers, you were suggesting, I think - it's gone off the screen now - but it was a reasonable conclusion that a Crisis Staff had been formed, and the implication of what you were saying was this, wasn't it, that it was a Crisis Staff of the nature that has been under discussion in the course of your evidence and referred to in your report?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an indication of an SDS Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, what I suggest to you, Ms. Hanson, is that it is clearly a different animal; that although it is described, in inverted commas, as "Crisis Staff" in the translation, and although it is apparently formed by the SDS heads of Zivinice, it is a different animal from the Crisis Staffs that we have been considering and which you have described in the course of your evidence.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tasks it deals with here are not tasks explicitly set out in the 19 December instructions, but Zivinice was a Serb minority, that is, Variant B municipality, and in the 19 December instructions, they say that Crisis Staffs there are to monitor the situation, adapt to circumstances and react, and this could be an example of a Crisis Staff reacting to a newly arisen situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, what I suggest to you, Ms. Hanson, is that there's a clear -- there's a clear unwarranted leap that you're making there, which is, because this particular type of Crisis Staff here is undertaking a task which is in the -- within the broad remit of a Crisis Staff proper, you're jumping to and unwarranted conclusion that this Crisis Staff being referred to is that kind of animal. And that's wrong, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an SDS Crisis Staff. It's doing things that are not directly linked to the 19 December instructions. I see no indication in any other evidence that the SDS at the municipal level had more than one kind of Crisis Staff. This document does say that a Crisis Staff was formed to deal -- to negotiate with the authorities, and this document is dated February.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, this is one of those situations. It's like when a government's got a problem, they set up a working party. Well, perhaps that's not the analogy because that's set up to avoid doing something. But it's a specific body set up to deal with the specific problem, ad hoc, here, immediately. This actual matter is to be sorted out by this "Crisis Staff" and that's its task.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this is -- I would just -- that is true, but this is specifically an SDS Crisis Staff, not a government thing. But yes, yes, the Crisis Staff, as reporting here to the president of the SDS and to the president of the Serbian Assembly, is dealing with these tasks -- seems to be dealing with these tasks mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And at the very least, because perhaps there will be some other evidence on this, Ms. Hanson, but on what you can read here and what you can see, at the very least, will you accept this: That one cannot reliably draw from this document that this Crisis Staff here was the type of Crisis Staff that we've been talking about throughout in accordance with, according to your evidence, the December 1991 instructions?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. We cannot read that from this document alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You've referred to Zivinice as a Serb minority municipality. Do you know what happened so far as control of Zivinice was concerned throughout the period of war?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it remained -- that it was under the Bosnian Muslim -- control of the Bosnian Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's what I've put to you.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It was, always was, and always remained throughout the war under Bosnian Muslim control.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you one additional question, Ms. Hanson, in respect of this? We see the word "Crisis Staff", and we see that it was immediately formed at a moment where an incident -- or at least an incident took place. Is it conceivable that this was a retarded follow-up of the instructions where a Crisis Staff might not have been formed right away, as perhaps it should have done under the 19 December instructions, but that the incident reminded those who were in a position to form a Crisis Staff that the incident was the trigger to do what they should have done already before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's a reasonable conclusion. It's not immediate -- there is no reference, as I said, in this document to the 19 December instructions, but it's a possible conclusion from that, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just asking whether it was conceivable, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would, then, the Crisis Staff be of the same kind as the others but formed at a -- well, at a little bit odd moment where the SDS heads were summoned to the side, which is usually not the place where you take these kinds of decisions, but would that -- I mean, I'd like to hear your opinion on whether that Crisis Staff, then, finally would be, by its nature, different from the other Crisis Staffs you discuss in your report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Given the make-up of the Crisis Staff as laid out in the 19 December instructions, that it would be local party leadership, that is, president, vice-president, people in the municipality who hold positions such as in the police, in the TO - pardon me - but also members of the Assembly and the Main Board, some of those people, reading what this Crisis Staff is doing, it seems that some of the membership would be the same. But whether these same people would continue to meet as such and carry out the tasks of the 19 December instructions, there's no evidence of that in this document. It seems that many of the same people would be on such a Crisis Staff, but it's just because they talk about -- discussing -- appointing a commander of the public security station, talk about having the JNA open a checkpoint. We know the Crisis Staff -- or the December 19 instructions also discussed appointing someone to coordinate with the SDA and HDZ, and they mentioned some coordination with that. It seems like there would be many of the same people but there is not enough in this document to say that it would then continue to operate as per the 19 December instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So there are still some doubts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I still have a question, madam, if you will allow me. I would like you to explain what you I wrote in the footnote on page 9. Zivinice, February 1992, the SDS Crisis Staff sent an appeal to Krajisnik and Karadzic among others to help resolve the crisis, et cetera. So far I have not understood what this means, and I have seen no illustration of the said appeal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You do not see it as an appeal, just simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could have a look at the translation as a whole, because we are now limited to just the part which is on the ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As I read it now, I see that -- I agree that over -- appeal is overstating. It's information about what's going on because they discuss problems with the negotiations and they're addressing it to a number of people. I -- I would say it's an appeal in the sense that they're addressing the people and some of the commanders of some of the organs involved, they're discussing a crisis, but I do not -- I agree -- or I do not see that it -- it is a direct appeal as such. It's described as a report, and it's describing some of the problems in the negotiations. A reasonable interpretation would be that it would -- because they're addressing the commands of some of these people, requesting their assistance, but it's not -- it's not as such -- appeal perhaps was not a good word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Do they request their attention or do they request their assistance or are they attracting their attention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the paragraph the citizens --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be first -- could we have a hard copy of this document in front of us, because I have difficulty from -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wonder whether -- whether I might, and adopting and incorporating Judge Hanoteau's question entirely, I wonder if I might pursue this matter in an attempt to clear it all up as quickly as I can? I promise I'm intending to incorporate Judge Hanoteau's question completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: If I break my promise, His Honour will no doubt revert to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: I will tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It is this, Ms. Hanson: I put it to you that what actually happened, as we see here, is that -- and we need to just look a little bit at the account here. What kicked all this problem off was a search of homes of Serb villagers. That's -- we see that in the second paragraph; right? That was the problem.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the search of Serb homes inspired the Serbs to block the highway.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Stay with me, Ms. Hanson, because I think what I just put to you is correct. It started with a search of the homes of the Serb villagers. Agreed?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It being --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The whole issue?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The barricades.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: This problem. This piece of paper stems from what started it all off, whatever the causes way back in history to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, it reads the immediate motive for such a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, search of homes. But I am saying this is a -- it's a report on the barricades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart will come to that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The search of homes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you answer first his question. So the origin was the search of homes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No doubt it all started in the fifteenth century but I'm going to take it from this date here. It started with a search of the homes of Serb villagers. In response to that or as a reaction to that, the Serb citizens then blocked the road?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's what happened next?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And that was in very colloquial, everyday terms, a crisis.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Right. So the SDS heads of Zivinice were summoned to the site. In other words, they got news pretty quickly that there was a problem. It's not a huge place.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: News travelled. They went there to try to work it out, as they say, to prevent things from getting out of role?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The citizens set the following conditions, one, two, three, four and so on. The citizens were the Serbs who were upset and concerned. Perhaps there were Muslims as well, but whatever. The citizens were the people who were directly affected and concerned with this incident?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Correct? They in their discussions -- there is apparent, isn't it? They in their discussions with these SDS heads who had been summoned to the site and went out there, they were saying, These are our conditions to lift the block of the road. So it was the Serbs clearly because they said, We'll lift the block of the road if you'll do the following, one, two, three, four?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Okay. Then over the page. The Crisis Staff, right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, we can agree that whatever it means, it's the same Crisis Staff at the top of page 2 of the English translation as we have been referring to in inverted commas earlier?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We've agreed about that. They had first negotiations that didn't result in deblocking. Now, the citizens -- so that's the same people supposedly broadly who have been setting conditions, negotiating about lifting the block, the citizens asked for republican government members to come out and they, according to this, sent letter to the Crisis Staff, Ejub Ganic; right? To the BH Assembly, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: To the government of Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, MUP, Tusico [phoen], et cetera, et cetera. So they were doing what citizens often do to in that situation. They were scatter-gunning or making sure that they sent their complaint to as many people as possible who might sort it out; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then the citizens have requested someone from the SDS leadership and from the Serb Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina to address them; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So if there was an appeal by anybody, it was really an appeal by those citizens, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an appeal by those Serbs and --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: There were. Serbs what do you mean by --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Serb citizens. Whether there was a separate appeal or whether this -- and/or whether this letter is part of that appeal because it is addressed to some of the people mentioned, they may have sent a separate appeal or this may be also channeling that appeal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Hanson, let's look at it. After all, it's very much the thesis of your report that documents mean what they say. It's -- it's really clear, isn't it? It says they sent a letter to the Crisis Staff. It's not a very happy reading of this document that this document is itself that letter, is it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to go back to your first comment, documents mean what they say they do. In reading any document, you have to take into account the context and understand that sometimes documents are written for self-serving purposes. I'm not saying it about this document as well, but I don't want to say that as a blanket statement for every document that I look at that they are to be taken exclusively on face value. In this case, I'm quite happy to look at this document in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, there isn't going to be dispute between us about that principle.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We can no doubt, can't we agree, about the principle that you read every document with common sense in the light of what you know about the context?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You agree about that. Reading this one, though, but starting -- do you agree, starting with at least the presumption that it means what it says. That's where you normally start, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Right. So it looks from that paragraph, because that's what it says, unless there's something to the contrary, it looks as if a letter had been sent by those Serb citizens to all those people --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. To all those people, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And in fact, there's an indication, a clear indication that it was a separate document because it records the letter as having been sent to the Crisis Staff, Ejub Ganic; correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I would take as a reference to the Crisis Staff of the Bosnian government at the republican level. Ejub Ganic was -- I don't know his specific position, but he was a member of the Bosnian government at the time. A different Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Correct, Ms. Hanson, correct. But the point is that this document is not addressed to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see what you mean. Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So it's clear that there was a separate document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I had not read that sentence at this time clearly enough when I made my earlier statement about this could be the request. It is clearly not. There is clearly a different letter involved, yes. I agree to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And I hope -- I hope Judge Hanoteau will fell that his question has been answered if I put this to you: So far as there was an appeal, it was essentially, in the first place, an appeal by those citizens. Ms. Hanson, I can put it to you and accept that, to a degree, it's reinforced by a document in this form that we see going to largely the same batch of addressees?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a letter to the same addressees discussing the problems, reporting on the problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But going back to your response to His Honour Judge Orie's question, where he put it to you, and Judge Orie phrased it very carefully, as always, and put it to you that it was conceivable that this was a belated - I'm not sure whether that was the exact word, but that was the sense - it was conceivable that this was a belated establishment of a Crisis Staff on the footing that, and I slightly paraphrase, on the footing that these people thought, Oh, ah, we failed to get round to setting up a Crisis Staff, and then they meet a situation, it reminds them, and they do set up a Crisis Staff. And Judge Orie put it to you, was it conceivable. You then said that was a reasonable conclusion, and His Honour Judge Orie rather reminded you that he only asked if you it was conceivable. And so we were trying to get clear whether you were saying that was your conclusion or whether it was a conceivable conclusion. So I am, with all that preamble, because it was a few minutes ago, going to ask you, Are you saying that in response to that possibility that was floated by Judge Orie as a testing question, are you saying that that was a conceivable position, or are you saying that your assessment is it was the probable situation?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had forgotten the first word that Judge Orie used. I would say it was a conceivable interpretation here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Is there any -- well, I have to press you. What is -- apart from the use of the phrase "Crisis Staff," what is there to support that conception, I suppose must be the right word?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a Crisis Staff formed by the leaders of the municipal SDS. It is a letter from the president of the SDS to the people mentioned, including the SDS leadership. At a minimum, it is a Crisis Staff of the Municipal Board of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Hanson, since, inevitably, your answer in response to His Honour's question dealing with conceivability, must contain an element of speculation, I would invite you to suggest, if that were what happened, or if it had been what happened, does it seem likely to you that Mr. Milic would have signed this document as the president of the SDS Zivinice instead of signing it as the president of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer that without speculating, but I would just add that I have seen no other instructions from the SDS leadership to -- about Crisis Staffs -- about forming Crisis Staffs different from the 19 December instructions. I don't see the SDS saying, Here's one set of instructions for these kind of Crisis Staffs, and here's instructions for a different kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, I'm not making it clear. That's a different point, really.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could repeat the question about Mr. Milic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I will. I'll put the point to you more explicitly, Ms. Hanson. If, and this is a hypothesis, after all, in response to your response -- based on your response to Judge Orie's questions, if it was a belated formation of the Crisis Staff in accordance with the instructions in December 1991, and the hypothesis is based on the footing that this was the SDS leaders in Zivinice realising that they hadn't got round to doing what they should have done before, so they're establishing the Crisis Staff towards the end of February, which they were supposed to have established in December, then one obvious step that Mr. Milic would have taken would have been to call his document a document coming from the Crisis Staff, to have signed himself as the president, assuming he had become the president, to have signed himself always the president of the Crisis Staff, and to thereby conveyed, admittedly in a slightly cosmetic, defensive way, but thereby conveyed the fact that yes, a Crisis Staff has been formed.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In February when this was written, the Crisis Staffs of the SDS were still essentially purely party organs. They had not yet assumed a public role, and this document is addressed, amongst others, to ministers in the Bosnian government and the head of the police, the Tuzla Corps. As we saw, those -- the role of the Crisis Staff at this time was still not open, especially in regard to Bosnian government ministries or the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Hanson, with respect, you can't have it both ways. The -- you're quite right. The dissemination of this document includes, doesn't it, apart from anything else, quite a few Muslims in positions of authority?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know offhand who were the presidents of the Municipal Assembly of Zivinice were or the police. But yes, it is a reasonable thing. It is going far beyond the SDS and going to open public organs of the Bosnian state. So there are very likely some Muslims, including Ejub Ganic, as mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I haven't checked, but a municipality such as Zivinice was a Muslim municipality --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would expect.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The chances of all these people being served so that --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. It's clearly not intended for -- yes, I'm sorry for speaking over you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, my fault.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we're actually agreeing. Yes, it's not limited to SDS. It's for public consumption. It is addressed to people who are quite likely Bosnian Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So, Ms. Hanson, it's even less likely, then, that the Crisis Staff referred to in this document is that Crisis Staff of the type which had not become public, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not informing the wider public here what kind of Crisis Staff it is. It put "Crisis Staff" in quotation marks. It is clearly a Crisis Staff of the Municipal Board of the SDS, but it is addressing an audience far beyond the SDS leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You see, I must put it to you, Ms. Hanson, your defence, not a complete defence in the end, but your defence of the possibility that this is a Crisis Staff proper - you understand what we mean by that, a December 1991 instructions type of Crisis Staff - is leading to a rather far-fetched position, which is that in a document of this nature, in response to a particular incident, widely disseminated to Serb and Muslim communities, the people in authority, Mr. Milic has, in some sort of slightly coded way, sought to communicate to the SDS leadership that yes, they have formed a Crisis Staff, but at the same time has, in a slightly disguised way, allowed that to be communicated to the Muslim community. That's a fantastic conclusion to reach, isn't it, from a practical everyday, common-sense point of view, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only repeat what I say in the footnote is borne out in this document, that it's a municipal -- SDS Municipal Board -- Crisis Staff of the SDS. Who is trying to talk to whom or convey what it's -- I do not think this document was written expressly to convey, in code or otherwise, information about the formation of a 19 December style Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm proposing to move on from this because one day perhaps somebody will come and give evidence about what really happened in Zivinice, but who knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, let's move on, then, please, to a different matter altogether. And it's the text which is linked to footnote 63. So we find this in paragraph 43 of your report. You say: "The Crisis Staffs --" you say: "The Crisis Staffs reported to central state organs of the Republika Srpska, including the Presidency, the --" I say Republika Srpska; you describe it as RS. That's a compendious term to cover the whole period, isn't it --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- regardless of the exact nomenclature?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: "The Crisis Staffs reported to central state organs of the RS, including the Presidency, the Assembly, and various Ministries ..." And at this point, I just want to ask you about one of those, because I'm not going to keep grinding through every footnote item by item. I assure Your Honours and Ms. Hanson I'm not going to do that, but let's take the Stari Grad example that you give which is over the page. Of course you're very helpful, you put it in alphabetical order so we find that easily. "The Crisis Staff centre requests to RS Ministry of Justice." You see that one?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I find that only in the master binder.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did not have that in the presentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And it's in master binder 4 at tab 192. The -- this actually has two -- sorry, Ms. Hanson. Are you --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm just looking at this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You're there with this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Just to recap very briefly what it is. It is -- on its face it does come from the president of Crisis Staff of Stari Grad, Mr. Krsmanovic, and it is addressed to the government of Republika Srpska MUP and Ministry of Justice, but you identify the Ministry of Justice in effect as the primary addressee; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And Ms. Hanson I'm not quarreling with that because it is -- the main point here is it is to request to start investigation proceedings against Mr. Delic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And it is for some corruption?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently, yes, that's what they're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But they're alleging criminal corruption?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The alienation of people's property and disintegration of a company.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then as a sort of an addendum but the last item linked to this there is piece of information that they have appointed Mr. Cecur as deputy manager of the same company.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The translation says deputy. The original says VD, which is usually "vrsilac duznosti," acting [In English], which I would take to be acting president.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So in fact what they have done is they have -- in a sense they have appointed Mr. Cecur to take over or replace Mr. Delic. It looks as if that's what's happened, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Delic is former manager; they have appointed an acting manager.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Perhaps you don't know for sure, Ms. Hanson, but it's a pretty reasonable inference from here that that's what's happened. They've kicked out Mr. Delic, and they want him to be the subject of criminal proceedings and they have put Mr. Cecur in in his place.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they kicked him out or not. He may have run off with the money. It's not clear why he is --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You're quite right about that possibility, of course.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The -- so this is -- there is a report to the ministry and to the government. There is a report of the appointment of Mr. Cecur as the new manager, the VD did you say I think?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: There is a report. Who would you -- from what you're telling the Trial Chamber about the structure of the Crisis Staffs and the links, there are three addressees here. Which is the -- which is the right target or who is the right addressee for such a piece of information coming from a Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ministry I would take to be a subset of the government in that the government included the minister. So I don't see them as necessarily different addressees, but in terms of what is the criminal procedure, how a charge should be investigated, I don't know the details of how a charge of corruption or embezzlement is to be treated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, I just suggest to you there that there's -- perhaps you can't say one way or another. It's pretty obvious that the Ministry of Justice is the right body or the right organ to whom to address a request to start investigation proceedings for these alleged criminal activities. That's not a serious issue, is it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't -- it's also addressed to the Ministry of the Interior, that is the police. I don't know the procedure for the investigation of crime, at what point the Ministry of Justice and the police are involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: All right. That's very fair, Ms. Hanson. You're basically saying you don't know the answer --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers kindly pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, you're invited and you as well, Ms. Hanson, to make a break between question and answer because you're speaking the same language and the interpreters might not be able to follow it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I was going to say thank you for the reminder, Your Honour, and then I forgot to make a break between what Your Honour was saying and my answer to Your Honour, so I will try to remember to do that. Thank you for the reminder anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm at least glad to hear that we're speaking the same language, Mr. Stewart. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, it's taken over completely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, in relation to the last point, supposing that -- it's a little bit of a hypothesis here, but what I'm asking you is from your examination of the materials and the evidence that you have given in relation to Crisis Staffs and communication of Crisis Staffs, if you had a municipal Crisis Staff that had appointed Mr. Cecur as the manager of this company, question number one, from all the documents you've seen, would you in fact expect a Crisis Staff even to bother to report the matter at all to any central organ of Republika Srpska or the SDS?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends, I think, on what the company would be. But if it was a purely local company, and I don't know what the abbreviation ZGP stands for, what kind of company it might be. Some were of more importance than others. But a routine appointment I have not seen other records of Crisis Staffs simply reporting an appointment of a company director as simply -- I have not seen such reports per se, just here we are reporting on whom we've appointed to a company.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you overall, Ms. Hanson, is this document is not really -- it's not really a report to any central organ. It is an action by the Crisis Staff, but it is to get criminal proceedings started. It's not a report, and the bit of report at the end is tacked on because it's a natural thing to tack on in those circumstances. If they're going to tell them they want an investigation of Mr. Delic, they've simply added on, that, By the way, we've replaced him. Does that summary of this document fit what you know and fit the reading?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a request, which is what I call it in my footnote, a request, but it is addressed, as we said, to number -- at least three bodies, two or three depending on how you describe them, at the republic level about events on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's just it's not a report. It's -- a report implies some accountability, doesn't it, and this itself is not a report, is it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is conveying information.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would think that the matter has been sufficiently explored as the Chamber does.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break until ten minutes to one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, may we look, please, at paragraph 38 now of your report. That's where you specifically refer to Mr. Krajisnik, notably the republic commissioner's report to Krajisnik, in his role as the member of the Presidency responsible for work of the republican commissioners. So may we look first, then, at the document in footnote 51, which I find in the master binder at -- I don't have a presentation binder reference, though I've got an uncomfortable feeling it might be in the presentation binder. Is that correct? Well, I am inviting that reference, Your Honour. I -- if that's readily to hand, that might be more convenient for all and sundry. Especially remind myself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you give us a number, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's master binder 3, tab 138.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, it's precisely because I know we have looked at it before in the course of your evidence that I know it must be in the presentation binder somewhere. Ms. Hanson, a key --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I think it's presentation tab 118.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The Presidency minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's the minutes of the Presidency of the 6th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's tab 118 in the presentation binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Then binder 3, 118. Thank you very much. It's really an alternative source for everybody. So It's 3, 138, and then it's master 3, and 118 of presentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, anyway, you've got the document in front of you. A key point here in this meeting as recorded and the basis of, really, most of the discussion was Dr. Koljevic's expressed position, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was -- what do you mean by his expressed position? I was looking at the actual agenda item where they divide the tasks, or are you on the first page of the agenda --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, you were, Ms. Hanson. But what I was putting to you is, just to reiterate, that, if you like, the central point and the key point from which most of the discussion from this meeting stemmed was Dr. Koljevic's expressed position which we find -- to point you there, we find under item 1.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see those as separate items of the agenda. Agenda item 1 is Koljevic. Agenda item 2 is positions on the initiative of the Muslims and Croats. There's various business. And agenda item 4 is division of work in the Presidency. I don't see that those -- the entire agenda stems from agenda item 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's have a look, then. Item 1. Perhaps you -- does that mean, then, that -- does that mean that, first of all, you have at some point read this whole document, but that more recently in connection with your evidence before this Trial Chamber, you have focused only on item 4?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- that's a good description.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, in that case, although it will take just a minute or two, so -- I'm sure you're a very quick reader, Ms. Hanson, I am going to invite you, and I won't read it into the record myself because that would be unnecessarily time-consuming, but to read the other items --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll read it --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- fairly quick so you'll --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- In the translation, just for --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Whichever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. I've scanned it quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: All right. So do you see, first of all, under item 1 - I don't want to grind through absolutely everything here - but at the beginning of item 1, in connection with the first item, Dr. Koljevic stated why he was discontented with the work of the Presidency. He was discontented with his own performance and he couldn't endure the work physically or psychologically. He was having family problems. And the efficiency, he made the general statement, the efficiency of the Presidency was low. You see all that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So he proposed that he resign from the Presidency, that he be appointed Minister of Foreign Affairs, and then the particular request that his family move to and was given an apartment in Belgrade. Then there's -- 4, we won't go into. I'm not suggesting it's unimportant, but it's not germane for present purposes. Then Dr. Plavsic spoke up against anybody resigning - counter-productive, harmful consequences, and so on. So she went along with the Belgrade suggestion. Dr. Branko Djeric said results significant, so he was saying, Well, paraphrasing, don't be too hard on yourself, Dr. Koljevic. And then the Presidency -- over the page, the Presidency operates without division of tasks --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, Ms. Hanson has gone through item 1. We have read item 1. Now you're repeating, more or less, aloud item 1 again. Could you please come to your point?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The -- and then -- but Dr. Karadzic -- I will skip. Dr. Karadzic stated, "must be discontented with our performance," important that even if we existed, even if we did nothing and so on and then in summary in the next paragraph Dr. Koljevic comes back to not agreeing that the work of the Presidency was good and so on. So so far, just in summary, then, it's not exactly a mea culpa, but Dr. Koljevic in a nutshell is saying I haven't been doing a good job. We haven't been doing a good job. Dr. Karadzic is saying well, actually we haven't been doing so bad a job overall, and Dr. Djeric is saying, and you, Dr. Koljevic, haven't been doing as bad a job as you say. Is that -- I just want to ask you first of all, from your reading of many, many documents in this case, does that broadly reflect a pattern that you've seen, that in the public statements Dr. Karadzic does tend to take a publicly -- and publicly within this sort of meeting as well take a more positive view and describe things as going well when others express a rather different view? Is that a pattern is that you have seen?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree that Karadzic does at times -- does generally take a positive view. He also does criticise and urge action in other places. As compared to others' views, I can't speak with confidence on that. I don't -- I'm familiar with this case of Dr. Koljevic's discontent, but I couldn't speak to others with any degree of certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Then we get to what I suggest to you is a key point here. Dr. Koljevic says, "He stressed that he could not control the republican commissioners and considered that as his failure." You see that, do you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, do I.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, that's clearly indicating isn't it that that was something that was his responsibility, his task, and in his view he not been able to perform it.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is saying that he wasn't able to do it. Djeric says earlier that there is not a division of tasks, so I don't see it as exclusively his task. He sees it as his failing. But that was his own exclusive task, I don't see that given Djeric's comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, you've interpreted Djeric's comments but what are next recorded as Dr. Koljevic's comments saying that the duration of the Presidency itself suggested that he was not the right person for that position, that he had reached the limits and could not carry on. Now, he's -- what do you say he's talking about there? Isn't he saying, I'm not the right person to be controlling these republican commissioners. I've failed?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sentence on the duration of the session, I think he's indicating he's tired, he's reached his limits. He's saying I cannot last this long. This discussion has gone on long enough. Perhaps he was suggesting he's on the verge of a collapse of some kind. That sentence regarding the duration of the session. I don't see those two sentences as directly related. He says he could not control the republican commissioners, but the second sentence I feel he's referring to how long they've been discussing right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, he clearly is in the first part, Ms. Hanson, we can agree about that. He's just had enough, hasn't he. But when he says he wasn't the right person for that position, those are plainly linked, aren't they, the previous sentence and that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I could read the original. The antecedent is not quite as clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Explain why. I, Ms. Hanson, like many people in this court can only work with the language we understand so -- and of course if you can explain more fully on the basis of the original, please do.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: [B/C/S spoken]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I wonder if you could give they that again, Ms. Hanson, because I hadn't had my headphones on and I wasn't quick enough to get the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would not have been different, Mr. Stewart, because I didn't hear any translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The length of the sessions of the Presidency speak for themselves. That this is not the right place for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, I suggest in view of what you were going to say wouldn't it be better if you were to read the previous sentence as well so we could get the two sentences together which I'm suggesting are the ones that may be linked?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. I'll just move to B/C/S. [Interpretation] He pointed out that he cannot handle the republican commissioners, and he considers this to be a failure on his part. The length of the session of the Presidency itself shows that that was not the right place for it and that he could not go any further. [In English] I don't know how it was translated but it seems he was saying the Presidency is not the place for me. I can't stand these long sessions. That is how I read the original as the most likely interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, what we've got at the moment is we've got in the translation, forgive me for half sitting, Your Honour, I'm trying to read two items at the same time, I hope Your Honours will forgive that. In the -- in the English translation which we had in the binder, it reads: "Suggested that he was not the right person for that position." That's the key phrase. And what we've got just now was: "That that was not the right place for it," which is not -- that second one is not -- I'm not criticising the interpretation, of course, I'm just saying it's the not so easy to see what he's getting at. So what -- how are you offering to explain this to the Trial Chamber, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The phrase "on nije za to mjesto" I would translate as "he is not for this place," that is, "this is not the place for him."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that what they hear now, "on nije za to mjesto," does indeed mean "he is not for that place."

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. That's most helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Do you say, then, Ms. Hanson, that there is now ambiguity about whether he's talking about the position as the person to control republican commissioners or position as a member of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I take it to mean he is referring to the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So there's no ambiguity as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that there's -- other interpretations are possible, but that one sentence, given those -- even -- even putting the two sentences together, I still think it's most likely that he's talking about the Presidency itself. I do not exclude the possibility of your interpretation, but I think simply he's saying, I can't last even through one session. It's not the place for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Did you -- sorry, I'll following the injunction to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, may I ask for one clarification. One time when you read it we have "the sessions" and the other time we have in translation "the session" of the Presidency. Of course the one would be different meaning than the other. The one being that -- I would say more or less the existence of the Presidency whereas the other is the sessions of. You are using "sessions" when you explain it. Could we clarify that? Could you perhaps explain why you take the plural?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The a genitive plural and a genitive singular are the same. He could be saying -- no, forgive me. It is not the same. It is definitely a genitive plural. It would be the length of this session would be "sjednica." So it's the plural here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask the interpreters whether they confirm this interpretation. Perhaps I should have asked you first but...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters please see the document? That would make things much easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That would be a reasonable request from the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I wouldn't expect anything else than a reasonable request from the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The phrase is in the centre of the screen, "sama duzina sjednica."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It's the plural note the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I hope it's understood we can't supply all these documents in advance because we don't know when an issue is going to arise. So I hope that's understood with apologies there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there's one thing. In the translation we also find the singular. That should then be the plural as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. It works, Your Honour, doesn't it, because with respect, because it wouldn't be very natural to say "the duration of the first session." One would say "this session." But it's clear from what the interpreters say that we're talking about plurals anyway, and then it be "the sessions." So --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, in any case, Ms. Hanson, as far as that goes it's a general complaint by Mr. Koljevic about the length of the meetings rather than the specific one. But the -- but, Ms. Hanson, he -- first of all, let's agree this. First of all, he does specifically mention and draw attention to control of republican commissioners as -- that's the one task that he specifically mentions in the context of his failure, his own adjudged failure.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He certainly mentions it. I'm just checking if it's the only one. Yes. So far it's the only one. He specifies that as his -- as his failure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Which, Ms. Hanson, in a sense -- well, you have the background. You've done the research. You've done this report so that's why you're being pressed for your interpretations of these items. That does strongly suggest, doesn't it, that that was very much his task?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of his tasks, yes. I can't exclude that he had others.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, Ms. Hanson, to make it clear, I'm note excluding that either.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But I'm talking about whose task it was. And you've confirmed that. So it suggests that that was very much his task. So if he was going, if that task were going to be attempted by somebody else, well, somebody else would have to be chosen, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In as far as the Presidency until this moment had set division of labour, which the other indications in this document is they didn't until now have a specific division of labour for all tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Hanson, may I suggest to you you're drawing that conclusion from what Mr. -- from what Dr. Djeric says, aren't you, about the Presidency operates without division of tasks?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: And also from agenda item 4 in which they set up a division of tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, agenda item 4, it may be your view, agenda item 4 doesn't show that the division of tasks is a new concept, does it? It just shows that for the future, the division of tasks is to be as set out in item 4.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I've seen no previous Presidency minutes setting out such a division of tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, that's a different matter, Ms. Hanson. I was going to ask you about this. From looking back at previous documents, have you been able to see any indication of who had responsibility? If we take the position before this document, from earlier documents have you seen any indication of who had either formally or as a practical matter responsibility for the republican commissioners?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Before this date, I see know -- I recall no discussion of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But also more widely, is there any material which indicates any member of the Presidency having responsibility for that task?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Previous to this -- previous to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Previous to this.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I do not recall any such indications.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Or separately any document indicating any actual or attempted performance of such a task by any member of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other than the appointments which we have seen appointing commissioners and confirming the composition of War Commissioners -- of War Commissions, I haven't seen such. I do not recall seeing what you refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That position, you'd agree, is in fact among other things consistent with Dr. Koljevic having had that task but seemingly failed to perform it.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't comment on his failure but --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, that's consistent. That is consistent with that position, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see his failure or success as -- I can't judge that from a lack -- from -- from no evidence. Every -- it is consistent with -- since I've seen nobody other than Karadzic until this point signing the appointments, because I believe, although I'll have to check, that the appointments signed by Krajisnik were in fact later, after this date, we see Karadzic appointing and signing the appointments of the commissioners. Other than that, I see nothing inconsistent with this statement of Koljevic or the implication of Koljevic that he was involved in the work of the commissioners, but I can't -- can't say more than that. It is consistent with him having had something to do with the work of commissioners.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's look at item 4, then, which is where you in effect started from for the purposes of your immediate evidence at this hearing.
